key_insight: A normal form for Pauli-based computation fully characterizes its adaptivity and entanglement, connecting it to one-way quantum computing as a time-reversed counterpart.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports distributed quantum computation and ahead-of-time compilation that can reduce entangling-gate overhead and quantum memory requirements.
method: Derive a normal form for Pauli-based computation.
Use its structure to analyze distributed computation and magic-state injection rates.
Efficiently identify unnecessary magic-state qubits and compile circuits ahead of execution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exponential improvement in detecting unnecessary magic-state qubits and average reductions of 50% in CNOT count and 40% in quantum memory on random quantum circuits, outperforming compared state-of-the-art compilers.
watch_item: Reported gains are averages on random circuits; benefits for practical workloads and hardware-specific constraints remain to be established.
paper_title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
